Question 1

Given that P(A)=0.5, P(A∩B)=0.4, and P(A∪B)=0.8, find P(B′).

a
0.4
b
0.8
c
0.5
d
0.7
e
0.3

decision.explanation: By the addition law, P(B)=P(A∪B)−P(A)+P(A∩B)=0.8−0.5+0.4=0.7. Therefore P(B′)=1−0.7=0.3.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Given that $P(A)=0.5,$ $P(A\cap B)=0.4,$ and $P(A\cup B)=0.8,$ find $P({B}^{′}).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ 0.8 & =0.5+P(B)-0.4 \\ P(B) & =0.8+0.4-0.5 \\ P(B) & =0.7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P({B}^{′}) & =1-P(B) \\  & =1-0.7 \\  & =0.3.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The addition law gives P(A∩B)=1/2+2/5−7/10=1/5. Thus P(A′∩B)=2/5−1/5=1/5. Taking the complement, P(A∪B′)=1−1/5=4/5.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(A\cap B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ \frac{7}{10} & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{5}-P(A\cap B) \\ P(A\cap B) & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{5}-\frac{7}{10} \\ P(A\cap B) & =\frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we construct the corresponding Venn diagram and shade the region $A\cup {B}^{′}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14064054/assets/5ecc7dae3e6b6e57ccd4a7b8907cb4dd20b0ece400a5768b747f3cb3da788e4b.png)

Finally, we have

$$
P(A\cup {B}^{′})=\frac{3}{10}+\frac{1}{5}+\frac{3}{10}=\frac{4}{5}.
$$
